Subject: Data custody + erasure confirmation request

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again — we're wrapping up the security review for our hosted API procurement and have a short set of clarifying questions attached (Orbis_QUESTIONNAIRE_v2.xlsx). Can you confirm the following for Redwood Hosted API as it will apply to our tenant: 

- Typical retention windows for request payloads (customer request & response bodies) and system logs
- Behavior and TTL for in-memory/KV caches used by the runtime
- Backup/snapshot retention and how/when backups are included/excluded from deletion requests
- Exact timeline once we request a tenant deletion: suspension window, purge job timing, and when data becomes unrecoverable
- Evidence we can provide for our auditors (S3 snapshot manifests, log export examples, SOC2/attestation links)

We're targeting signature next week; we need the above answers to close our security sign-off. If any of this is contractually negotiable (shorter purges, extended retention), flag it and we'll surface it to procurement.

Appreciate a quick reply — even high-level — and we can follow up with a call if needed.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Security, Orbis Analytics

Hi Samantha — thanks for sending this over. I've put together initial answers below and attached a short summary (Redwood_HostedAPI_Data_Retention_Summary.pdf). I'm looping in our infra/security engineers (Kimberly, Jonas) to confirm the backups and deletion timeline details; I'll follow up with a final authoritative answer within 48 hours.

High-level answers (hosted API, default behavior unless the account has a negotiated addendum):

- Request payloads (request/response bodies): retained for up to 30 days by default for debugging and support, then purged from hot storage. Customers may opt-in to shorter retention via API flags or contract.
- System logs (audit/ingest/usage): retained for 90 days in compressed storage for troubleshooting and billing reconciliation.
- KV/in-memory cache (prefix/KV & runtime cache): ephemeral by default. Default TTL is ~6 hours; configuration allowed up to 48 hours for performance reasons. Cache entries are not used as a primary persistence mechanism.
- Backups & snapshots: encrypted snapshots are taken for platform resiliency; default snapshot retention is 14 days in the primary region.
- Tenant deletion workflow: upon an authorized deletion request we suspend access immediately, schedule purge jobs that target active storage within 7 days, and begin backup retention discontinuation. Final irreversible removal from all replicated systems (including backup chains where possible) is typically completed within 30-45 days depending on snapshot retention/replication windows.
- Evidence for auditors: we can provide S3 object manifests, deletion job runbooks, and our SOC 2 attestation link (attached).

Attachments: Redwood_HostedAPI_Data_Retention_Summary.pdf (PDF, 45KB); SOC2_Attestation_URL.txt (link stub)

Action items: 
- @jonas.weber: confirm exact backup scrub window and how that translates into final irrecoverability (we typically have a 14-day snapshot retention but need to call out offsite/immutable snapshot behavior).
- @kimberly.park: can you confirm whether any of the default retention windows differ for us-east vs eu regions?

Samantha — will finalize and send an answer you can attach to your packet. If you'd like a 20-minute call to walk through, I'm happy to set one up.

Thanks,

Thanks for the ping — quick clarifications from the infra side to make Mateo's draft definitive: 

- KV/runtime cache: default TTL is 6 hours (hot cache). Platform settings allow an enterprise-configurable window up to 48 hours; extending TTL is only available under dedicated or contract terms. Cache is not written to persistent object store and is excluded from backups.
- Request payloads: we keep unredacted request/response bodies in hot storage for 30 days by default; these are then moved to ephemeral cold storage for an additional short troubleshooting window and ultimately deleted. For regulated customers we can set a shorter window or log-only mode (no request body retention).
- System logs and audit trails: 90-day retention by default (audit events, billing records). We can export logs on request into a customer-owned S3 for long-term retention.
- Backups & snapshots: primary snapshots are rotated with 14-day retention. However, some offsite immutable snapshots (created for disaster recovery) can persist longer (up to 45 days) depending on region and replication policy. During a deletion workflow we mark backups for exclusion from future replication and queue them for scrub once their retention window expires.
- Deletion timeline (hosted API): 
  * Day 0: Account suspension and initiation of deletion workflow upon authorized request.
  * Day 0-7: Purge jobs target active object stores and search indexes; most hot/cold data is removed in this window.
  * Day 7-30: Backups and snapshots enter scrub queue; deletion from primary backups occurs as snapshots rotate out.
  * By Day 45: Final irrecoverability for the majority of cases (some remote immutable snapshots may reach full expiry up to 45 days).

Note: these are the platform defaults. For enterprise deals we document exact windows in the Data Residency/Addendum and can shorten or extend them as negotiated. We sign off on forensic evidence (manifests, deletion run logs) under NDA.

-Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Samantha — thanks for the patience and for the checklist. Per Jonas' verification below, here's the consolidated, authoritative response you can attach to your security packet. I've also attached the retention summary PDF and included links to our SOC2 attestation and a sample deletion job manifest.

Consolidated answers (Redwood Hosted API — default, unless modified in contract):

1) Request payloads (request/response bodies)
- Default retention: 30 days in hot storage for debugging and customer support. After 30 days request bodies are removed from hot storage; a short, temporary cold retention may be used for diagnostics but not more than an additional 14 days without explicit customer agreement. Customers may opt for 'log-only' mode (no request body retention) via contract or API settings.

2) KV/in-memory cache
- Default TTL: 6 hours. Configuration: up to 48 hours for enterprise contracts. Cache contents are not included in persistent backups.

3) System logs and audit trails
- Default retention: 90 days. We can provide log exports to a customer-owned S3 for longer-term retention; exports can be automated.

4) Backups & snapshots
- Primary snapshot rotation: 14 days. Offsite/immutable disaster recovery snapshots may persist up to 45 days depending on region/replication. During a deletion request we mark backups to cease replication and queue them for scrub at the end of their retention window.

5) Tenant deletion workflow and timeline
- Day 0: Receipt of authorized deletion request; tenant suspended and admin/API access disabled.
- Day 0-7: Purge jobs execute against active object storage, caches, and indexes.
- Day 7-30: Backup/snapshot rotation continues; backups marked for scrub are removed as snapshots expire.
- By Day 45: Final irrecoverability in the general case; some remote immutable snapshots may take longer only in rare disaster recovery configurations (we document this per-account).

Evidence we can provide:
- S3 object manifest snapshots for deletion jobs (sample provided in Drive link).
- Deletion job run logs and runbook excerpts (available under NDA).
- SOC 2 Type II attestation link: https://drive.redwood/soc2/attestation-2028 (also included in SOC2_Attestation_URL.txt).

Attachments: Redwood_HostedAPI_Data_Retention_Summary.pdf; SOC2_Attestation_URL.txt

Next steps:
- If Orbis requires shorter or contractually guaranteed purge timelines, we can add a Data Residency Addendum (DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/REDWOOD/ORB-ADDENDUM-2029).
- Happy to arrange a 20-minute call this week to walk through the evidence package with your auditors. Please suggest times.

Best regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
